application_type_full: Approval of details reserved by a condition (discharge)
decision_conditions: <p>In the absence of satisfactory details, including samples and drawings of all external materials forming part of the development approved under planning permission 2021/1831, the Local Planning Authority is unable to assess whether the proposed materials would achieve a high-quality architectural finish. Furthermore, the submitted details include elements that do not form part of the approved scheme and are subject to separate assessment. The submitted information therefore fails to satisfy the requirements of Condition 5 of planning permission 2021/1831 and is contrary to Policy LP1 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020) and Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021).</p>

In the absence of sufficient details relating to the proposed sustainable drainage measures, including site-specific specifications, construction details and supporting technical information demonstrating the design, capacity and implementation of the proposed SuDS features, the Local Planning Authority is unable to determine whether the development would provide an appropriate sustainable drainage system or achieve a reduction in surface water runoff. The submitted information therefore fails to satisfy the requirements of Condition 3 of planning permission 2021/1831 and is contrary to Policy LP53 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020) and SI 12 of the London Plan (2021).

<p>In the absence of sufficient details relating to the proposed flood resilience and resistance measures, including specifications, layouts, levels and construction details demonstrating how such measures would be implemented on site, the Local Planning Authority is unable to determine whether the development would be adequately safeguarded against surface water flood risk. The submitted information therefore fails to satisfy the requirements of Condition 4 of planning permission 2021/1831 and is contrary to Policy LP53 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020) and Policy SI 12 of the London Plan (2021).</p>
